model: HVEA Pyramid — Windows 11 variant (Paper II Section 4.2 test environment)

tiers.name: Attribution and Environment Anchor
tiers.function: Establishes identity and configuration context. All higher tiers rely on Tier I for interpretive stability.

tiers.name: Primary Evidentiary Object Layer
tiers.function: Contains the semantic focus of investigation: user-generated artifacts and outward interaction indicators.

tiers.name: Behavioral Contextualization
tiers.function: Bridges attribution and payload: execution chronology, application interaction, deletion residues.

tiers.name: System-Level Independent Corroboration
tiers.function: Provides structural validation independent of semantic payload interpretation.

layers.name: System & Hardware Baseline
layers.purpose: Establish the operating environment required for interpretation (OS version, file system type, disk layout, installed-program baseline, system time configuration).

layers.name: User & Machine Identity Context
layers.purpose: Defines attribution scope and identity anchoring (user accounts/SIDs, profile directories, registry system hives, group membership, machine identifiers).

layers.name: User Content (Evidentiary Payload)
layers.purpose: Recover primary evidentiary objects under identity attribution. Contains documents, media, financial records, archives, downloads.

layers.name: Network Interaction Presence
layers.purpose: Identify boundary-crossing activity and external interaction context. Captures host indicators, communication traces, network profile artifacts.

acquisition_paths.note: NetworkList and Tcpip keys live here; co-acquired with Layer A SYSTEM hive.

layers.name: Execution & Recency Telemetry
layers.purpose: Reconstruct execution chronology linking identity to payload access. Prefetch, Shimcache, Amcache, recent files, shortcut traces.

layers.name: Browser & Application Interaction
layers.purpose: Contextualize acquisition, research, and dissemination behavior. History, cookies, web storage, IndexedDB, typed URLs, bookmarks, download metadata.

layers.name: Deletion & Transient Residues
layers.purpose: Detect deletion intent and artifact lifecycle behavior. Recycle Bin entries, temporary artifacts, thumbnail cache, cleanup traces.

acquisition_paths.note: Recycle Bin residues may persist in unallocated space after emptying.

layers.name: Event Logs (System Temporal Chronology)
layers.purpose: Independently corroborate authentication, boot, and service chronology. Security, system, application event records.

layers.name: NTFS Metadata (Structural Ground Truth)
layers.purpose: Validate file lifecycle and structural consistency independent of semantic interpretation. $MFT entries, MAC timestamps, structural attributes.

layers.name: USN Journal & File Change Chronology
layers.purpose: Reconstruct fine-grained file-system change chronology and concealment behavior. $UsnJrnl entries, structural change indicators.

acquisition_paths.note: $LogFile is explicitly excluded — supports transactional crash recovery, not evidentiary chronology.

dependencies.rationale: Identity context (B) is interpreted within the operating environment baseline (A). Without A, B's SIDs and profile paths lack environmental grounding.
User content (C) requires identity attribution from B. Documents and downloads cannot be reliably associated with a specific user without B's SID and profile context.
Network interaction (D) requires attribution boundary from B to associate boundary-crossing activity with an identity.
Execution telemetry (E) links identity to payload access; the identity anchor is B.
Execution telemetry (E) is interpretively about access and handling of payload (C). Without C, E events lack semantic targets.
Browser interaction (F) requires user attribution from B; browser profiles live under user-account paths.
Deletion residues (G) reflect post-creation handling of payload (C). G's interpretive value depends on what was deleted relative to C.
Recycle Bin entries are SID-scoped; G requires B for user attribution.
Three-source convergence pattern from Paper II: SAM last-login (B), NIC LastWrite (D), event log session record (H) converge to corroborate session attribution.
Three-source convergence pattern: H corroborates D's network presence by recording the session in which network activity occurred.
Event logs (H) anchor execution telemetry (E) chronologically: H's logon session timestamps validate E's Prefetch timestamps.
NTFS metadata (I) provides structural ground truth for payload (C): MAC timestamps in $MFT validate semantic claims about file creation and modification.
I corroborates G: $MFT entries persist after deletion and validate Recycle Bin chronology.
USN journal (J) confirms creation, modification, and deletion chronology for payload (C). Paper II walkthrough cites $UsnJrnl as the precise timestamp source for archived files.
J independently corroborates G: $UsnJrnl records deletion events with reason codes, validating Recycle Bin's claim about what was deleted and when.
I (MFT) and J (USN journal) provide complementary structural views; J references MFT entries by record number.

convergence_patterns.name: Three-source session convergence
convergence_patterns.function: Paper II's defensible reconstruction standard: SAM last-login (B), NIC LastWrite (D), and event log session record (H) agreeing within 30 seconds corroborate session attribution and chronology.

convergence_patterns.name: Payload lifecycle corroboration
convergence_patterns.function: User content (C) validated by NTFS metadata (I) and USN journal entries (J) to confirm creation, modification, and deletion chronology independent of semantic claims.

notes: Paths reflect Windows 11 conventions confirmed against the W11_HVEA_14D controlled image (Paper II Section 4.2). User profile layout: /Users/<name>/. Event logs in /Windows/System32/winevt/Logs/*.evtx. Recycle bin at /$Recycle.Bin/<SID>/. Browser data under /Users/<name>/AppData/Local/{Google/Chrome,Microsoft/Edge}/User Data/.
